title: Controlled fault-injection evaluation of verifier-guided LLM repair on vendor CLIs (paired design)
research_question: Does a deterministic verifier-guided LLM repair pipeline reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared to blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults across Cisco and Juniper task templates?
confirmatory_hypotheses: Verifier-guided repair will yield a higher proportion of configurations that pass the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and simulator-based compliance check than blind repair on the same injected faults (guarded > baseline).

With n = 40 paired tasks the paired difference in verifier pass rates is estimable; a two-sided exact paired test will detect an absolute guarded-minus-baseline difference of approximately 30 percentage points or larger under the preregistered assumptions.
Verifier-guided repair will not increase harmful over-repair events beyond the prespecified safety threshold (<= 5% absolute increase).
exploratory_questions: How do pass-rate improvements vary by fault class (e.g., missing BGP neighbor vs. ACL order inversion)?
What proportion of repairs produce substantive intent-changing edits flagged by the frozen harmful-change rules (exploratory descriptive only)?
benchmark_scope: Controlled fault-injection vendor-CLI task bank (Cisco + Juniper) constructed from public configuration templates
Task bank limited to the 40 preregistered controlled-fault indices (1..40) generated by deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1
sampling_plan: Preregistered controlled-challenge, paired design using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Confirmatory task_count fixed at exactly 40 (task indices 1..40). For each task: one deterministic shared controlled-fault candidate generated by deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1 (one source_generation call per task), followed by two repair episodes (baseline blind repair, guarded validator-guided repair). Fault assignment is deterministic and outcome-independent (fault_assignment_seed=17). One initial model generation per task is preregistered and shared unchanged across paired conditions; runtime sampling parameters for each model call will be recorded in the execution manifest. Total confirmatory model-call budget = 120 (adapter-mandated).
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect for planning: ~30 percentage-point absolute paired difference. With n=40 and two-sided alpha=0.05, approximate detectable absolute paired differences ≈30 percentage points given nontrivial discordant-pair rates (~0.30); smaller effects have reduced power. Post hoc exact detectable-effect curves will be reported conditional on observed discordant counts. Sensitivity analyses include treating technical failures as failures and reporting detectable-effect curves under those assumptions.
exclusion_rules: Apply analysis-executor default 'complete_pair_primary': exclude a task pair from primary analysis only if both condition executions for that task fail for infrastructure reasons.
Document and report each exclusion with cause; exclusions do not alter preregistered sample size unless the adapter contract cannot be satisfied (see stopping_rule).
missingness_plan: Technical-execution failures are logged and classified. Primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs with incomplete executions) and reports the number and cause of exclusions. A sensitivity analysis treats missing repair outputs as failed repairs (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity) and is reported alongside the primary result.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 (primary_estimand_id = 'paired_binary_analysis_v1'). Primary test: exact paired binary test (McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial test) on combined success flag (vendor-CLI deterministic verifier pass AND simulator-based compliance pass). Report: discordant-pair counts (guarded-only success, baseline-only success), absolute risk difference with 95% CI, and two-sided exact p-value. Secondary analyses: per-fault-class descriptive risk differences with CIs (exploratory), harmful-overrepair counts and proportions, and model-call / latency cost analysis (model_call_cost_per_avoided_failure) with bootstrap CIs. Report instrumentation: model-call counts, elapsed wall-clock per episode, and runtime sampling parameters for each model call. Sensitivity analyses per registered options: (1) treat technical failures as exclusions (primary), (2) treat technical failures as failures (sensitivity). All raw artifacts, logs, and hashes will be archived and linked to reported numbers.
multiplicity_plan: Single predefined primary paired test (no multiplicity adjustment). All subgroup and per-fault-class analyses are exploratory and labeled as such; CIs provided but no confirmatory claims derive from exploratory analyses.
contamination_plan: Risk factors: potential overlap between public template fragments and model training data, and verifier↔simulator mismatch. Detection procedures: deterministic string-match scanning of generated tasks/faults against archived task bank; pre-confirmatory verifier↔simulator concordance validation on a disjoint set (not 1..40). Flagging rules: (a) flag tasks where verifier passes but simulator fails; (b) flag repairs that remove or disable lines listed in frozen 'protected-intent' schema. Analysis treatment: primary success requires both verifier AND simulator agreement; disagreements reported descriptively and presented in sensitivity tables (verifier-only, simulator-only). Report residual contamination uncertainty in limitations.
stopping_rule: If at runtime the registered adapter planning contract hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 cannot be satisfied (for example, required multiples-of-40 task_count or model-call budget constraints, or adapter-mandated deterministic task-indexing cannot be honored), stop the execution and abort the confirmatory run; record the cause, timestamp, and all logs. No silent adapter substitution is permitted.
planned_outputs: Full execution manifest and raw artifacts (configs pre/post, tokenized diffs, verifier/simulator traces, model-call metadata, runtime sampling parameters, hashes)
Statistical results file (paired counts, CIs, p-values, sensitivity analyses)
IEEE two-column short-paper LaTeX source and compiled PDF (<=5 pages) including mandatory Disclosure Statement
NotebookLM presentation brief (machine-readable) prepared for post-acceptance
Autonomous revision log and provenance hashes
